entries.claim_consumed: Under preparation noncontextuality, V + P <= 1 holds for every preparation that belongs to a realized quadruple satisfying exactly the PRL's Eqs. (10)-(11) (A21-orbit realizability), relative to the fixed which-way measurement Z and the fixed which-phase measurement X; P = |<Z>| and V = |<X>| for that fixed X; the operational equivalence of Eq. (11) holds over all measurements on the carrier (Eq. 8). The PRL's main result is its Eq. (12), p. 4; the companion's Props. V.1 (theory level) and V.2 (experiment level) restate it. Proof: App. A, Eqs. (A1)-(A33); tightness: Eqs. (A35)-(A38); alternative derivation: App. B.
conditions: single-system prepare-measure scenario with two binary-outcome measurements (p. 2)
operational equivalence over all possible measurements (Eq. 8)
no outcome-determinism assumption; reduction to deterministic ontic states via the PRL's ref. [41], checked independently by the reader as a linear convex decomposition
entries.proof_followed: All steps followed on paper by the reader: the parametrizations (A13), (A18), (A23), the ranges (A14)-(A27) and (A28)-(A33), the tightness distributions and the reduction to four ontic states.

caveats.text: V in the consumed claim is |<X>| for a FIXED recombination setting X (companion Eq. 7), the which-phase predictability. It is not the contrast over a varying phase used for the complementarity benchmark of section 3.5. The orbit-realizability quadruple must be certified relative to the same X that is used for V.

'Equal predictabilities up to sign' (frozen L246) must be read as all three sign-flipped partners of Eq. (10), paired by the equivalence of Eq. (11). Section 5.3's certification 'over the whole of Acc' (L468-469) matches Eq. (8) only if Acc contains every carrier measurement.

The result covers single-shot prepare-measure with preparation noncontextuality only. Use in sequential, transformation (T3) or composite settings, or on a carrier correlated with a marker (carrier marginals treated as preparations), is MR-1's own obligation and is not supplied by the source.

The companion states Props. V.1-V.2 as 'if and only if'. The PRL proves the direction 'noncontextual implies bound' (App. A) and scenario-level tightness (App. B and its ref. [41]); it does not prove the theory-level converse of Prop. V.1. MR-1 consumes only the proved direction. The frozen phrase 'their Props. V.1-V.2, proved in Catani et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 129, 240401 (2022)' (L247) is to be read as covering that direction only.
p. 8 has 'epsilon'' = epsilon'; per (A13) it should be epsilon'' = -epsilon. It does not affect the result.
The three-measurement bound Eq. (C7) has no analytic proof in the source (a computer-algebra check is reported). MR-1 does not use it.

agreement_with_frozen_text: P = |P(L) - P(R)| = |<Z>| agrees with companion Eq. (6) (frozen L244).
'Quantum states with 0 < V < 1 on the curve exceed' is supported for pure states on V^2 + P^2 = 1: the bound meets that circle only where |<X>| = 1 or |<Z>| = 1 (PRL p. 5).
'No bound on V + D is claimed' (frozen L251-252) is consistent: the source treats only two measurements on one system.
CC4 returning no W1 is consistent: the stabilizer theory 'precisely saturates' the bound, and PRL p. 12 ties the octahedral state space to epistemic restriction.
entries.contradiction_check: NO. No load-bearing assumption of the frozen text is contradicted; the caveats above are scope statements.

entries.claim_consumed: T7 form for a single prepare-and-measure system: operational equivalences are defined over all measurements (respectively preparations) and made operational through a set assumed tomographically complete; secondary procedures are convex mixtures of primaries (and, for measurements, post-processings), chosen by a linear program to satisfy the equivalences exactly (SI Note 3, eqs 22-27); the inequality A <= 5/6 (eqs 6 and 8, p. 3) is derived without outcome determinism or noiseless measurements (SI Note 2, eqs 7-18) and refutes the conjunction of preparation and measurement noncontextuality; statistical equivalence relative to a set of measurements does not imply it relative to all measurements (SI p. 15).
conditions: ontological-model framework with mixtures represented as mixtures (eq. 1; SI eq. 12)
both preparation noncontextuality (SI eq. 6) and measurement noncontextuality (SI eq. 5) are assumed; a preparation-noncontextual, measurement-contextual model reaches A = 9/10 (SI Fig. 3)
tomographic completeness of the fiducial sets (SI eqs 3-6), tested by a GPT fit and called by the authors the most significant remaining loophole (p. 6)
acknowledged loopholes also include fair sampling, multiphoton events, polarization-spatial coupling and the absence of a rigorous p-value bound (SI p. 17)

caveats.text: Section 5.3 supplies tomographic completeness only relative to Acc, by definition. If stage 1 certifies equivalences through a finite subset of Acc, it owes a proved completeness lemma relative to Acc; and the residual assumption that Acc exhausts the relevant physical procedures remains, which is the source's own loophole.

The source is prepare-and-measure only; it has no transformation, sequential or adaptive inequality. T7's transformation clause ('T3's undo enters as a transformation') and the adaptive continuations draw on the source for form only, not for content.

AW-MR3 cites 'Mazurek et al. 2016 on inexact operational equivalences' for the relativity of equivalences to the access. The relativity point comes from the source's tomographic-completeness passage (SI p. 15); enlarging the test set can only dissolve equivalences between fixed procedures, and 'create' is supported only through new mixtures when the procedure set is enlarged (p. 4).
A W1 violation of an inequality of this form refutes the conjunction of preparation and measurement noncontextuality; it is not to be labelled preparation contextuality alone.
Secondary procedures require convex mixing to be available in Acc as a sourced procedure, consistent with convention c1.

entries.contradiction_check: NO. MR-1's universal quantification over Acc is the stronger, in-model form of the source's completeness assumption; the caveats above are scope statements.

claim_consumed: B-a: for a two-dimensional system, an explicit deterministic model, eq. (3), p. 448 (outcome alpha + |beta| sign(lambda|beta| + |beta_z|/2) sign X, with lambda uniform on [-1/2, 1/2]), reproduces every single-measurement expectation for a pure psi; its dispersion-free states have additive expectation values only for commuting operators (p. 449); not contextual in the Kochen-Specker sense

B-b: for state-space dimension greater than two, no dispersion-free state satisfies additivity of expectation values for commuting operators (section V, pp. 450-451; Gleason corollary; 'it is here that we need three dimensions at least')

B-c: in any dimension, an explicit deterministic contextual model (p. 451; hidden variable 0 < lambda <= 1; P_n gives 1 iff lambda_(n-1) < lambda <= lambda_n) reproduces the single-context statistics; the result for a given P_n 'depends also on the choice of the others'; the tacit noncontextuality assumption is named in the diagnosis that the result 'may reasonably depend ... on the complete disposition of the apparatus'
conditions: B-a: single measurements only; no measurement dynamics; no physical significance attributed to lambda (p. 448)
B-b: continuity argument over all vectors; constrains value assignments to all rays, not a finite set
B-c: called 'very artificial' by Bell; the lambda_n are built from psi's quantum expectations

caveats.text: Disturbing readout: partial. Outcome dependence on context is supported, but no measurement dynamics and no post-measurement state are given ('we enter upon it no more than is strictly necessary'); the section VI Bohm sketch (pp. 451-452) is not a disturbance model. Disturbing marker: none; no marker, record system or sequential readout appears.

The models are built from psi's own quantum expectations, so they are of the CC8 kind and agree with PC-Q on single measurements by construction. A CC2 instance is distinguished from CC8 only by a K1-fixed construction, which this source does not supply.

caveats.kind: scope caveat (dimension; inference of the reader, not a claim in Bell)
caveats.text: On the two-dimensional carrier alone, model B-a is not Kochen-Specker contextual; a KS-type obstruction needs dimension at least three, for example carrier together with marker (dimension four).
Bell does not treat preparation contextuality; Corollary U2 rests on Spekkens 2005 and is not affected.

agreement_with_frozen_text: The CC2 row (L569) agrees in part: a contextual deterministic model is supplied, a disturbing readout and a disturbing marker are not, matching the owner's warning in comment 6553497955.

Bell's results are functions of the hidden state together with the apparatus; in OI the apparatus is internal to S, consistent with Proposition A1 (L280) and with 'Under K1 the Kochen-Specker-type deterministic class contains frozen-interface-type models' (L562), which Bell does not address.
Bell's footnote 19 records a nonlocality proof found after completion; consistent with the CC2 row's 'T6 under K2 is not available to OI' (L569).
entries.contradiction_check: NO. Bell p. 451 (dependence 'on the complete disposition of the apparatus') and frozen A1 ('with internal settings, every record ... is a function of s_0') are compatible.

claim_consumed: M-a: the theorem's assumptions: value definiteness and eigenvalue values (section II, pp. 7-8), functional composition (eqs. 1-3, p. 9), and noncontextuality, named on p. 18 as the tacit assumption that an observable gets the same value whichever commuting set it is measured with
M-b: the four-dimensional square (section V, pp. 15-16): no assignment to its nine observables satisfies those assumptions, for any state
M-c: deterministic models escape the theorem only through context or apparatus dependence (section X, p. 24); a necessity statement, not a construction
conditions: the theorem is state-independent for dimension at least three (fn 11) and impossible in dimension two (fns 12, 17)
M-b applies to any model that assigns values to all nine observables of a carrier-marker system of dimension four

caveats.text: No contextual deterministic model with disturbing readout and no marker extension is constructed; the only explicit model is Bell's two-dimensional noncontextual one (section III). Disturbance is discussed only conceptually (p. 3; pp. 18 and 24).

Mermin's contextuality is measurement contextuality of value assignments; Corollary U2 rests on Spekkens 2005 preparation contextuality. This source does not substitute for U2's citation; there is no conflict.
'Kochen-Specker-type deterministic model' (L569) is ambiguous: by the theorem, such a model cannot be noncontextual beyond dimension two; in CC2 it is read as a contextual deterministic model.

Claims M-a and M-c in its all-rays form are also supported by Bell 1966 (LIT-4: B-b, B-c) and are usable. Claim M-b, and M-c restricted to a finite menu of observables, rest on this source alone and are blocked until the errata text is read. No CC2 decision rests on a Mermin claim alone before then.

agreement_with_frozen_text: The no-go side of CC2 (L569) agrees; the model itself must be supplied at stage 1.
Records that are functions of the complete state, apparatus included (A1, L280), are the context-dependent deterministic models section X permits; consistent with L562. Mermin says nothing about OI.

Corollary U3 (L345): Bohm 'deterministic with records functions of configuration given the guiding wave' agrees with Mermin p. 23 ('hidden variables are simply the real configuration space coordinates ... guided ... by the wave function'), which the paper asserts rather than derives.

corrections.corrected_value: kind 'scope caveat (psi-ontic construction)'; text: Bell's spin-1/2 model, eq. (3), is psi-ontic: its ontic state (psi, lambda), with lambda on a continuum, fixes the outcome of every single measurement alpha + beta.sigma on the system, so it is not a finite-menu A-realization of the CC8 kind; it reproduces the quantum single-measurement statistics by construction. The p. 451 contextual model is also psi-ontic and per state: its ontic state is (psi, lambda) with 0 < lambda <= 1, its thresholds lambda_n are cumulative quantum expectations in psi of the projectors one apparatus measures, it is defined for every such context with an order fixed by the set of projectors, and it reproduces the single-context quantum statistics by construction. Neither model is a K1-fixed construction, so no CC2 instance is supplied by this source.
corrections.reason: 'Per-law, CC8 kind' overstates: CC8 is a finite-menu realization of a stated law, while Bell's models are psi-ontic and cover every single measurement (respectively every context) on the system. The conclusion that no K1-fixed CC2 construction is supplied stands.
